title: Cross-functional SLO sandbox prototype brief
content:
Context and intent:

This is a compact working brief for a cross-functional sandbox pilot to validate operational changes to model-serving SLOs (latency & availability) without touching prod traffic. The sandbox is intended to be a safe lab for testing instrumentation, rollout policies, fallback behaviors, and SLO-driven automation (alerting, autoscale heuristics, and error-budget gating).

Why this exists (problem statement):
- We frequently tune SLO thresholds and rollout policies for model-serving routes but lack a fast, realistic environment to validate the end-to-end effects (obs, runbooks, automation).
- Small changes in batching/quantization/routing can have non-linear effects on tail latency and cache hit behavior; we need a repeatable workflow to exercise those changes and capture signals.
- Current experiments are scattered (ad-hoc load tests in infra, ad-hoc dashboards) and do not exercise cross-team handoffs.

Primary goals for the prototype (success criteria):
1) Demonstrate a sandbox end-to-end run that: applies a config change -> injects synthetic traffic -> collects telemetry -> triggers an alert when the synthetic SLI crosses a threshold -> validates runbook and rollback path.
2) Produce a reproducible experiment playbook (doc + scripts) that any feature team can run in < 90 minutes.
3) Surface at least three hidden observability gaps (missing signals, false positives, tracing blindspots) with remediation proposals.
4) Validate at least one automation hook (error budget pause, auto-fallback to smaller model variant) in the sandbox.

Scope (what is in / out):
- In: a single representative model-serving route (text-generation v2), a dedicated GPU tenant in the dev cluster, synthetic traffic generator, metric/trace dashboards, alerting rules cloned from staging, a minimal runbook and rollback script.
- Out: customer-facing capacity tests at scale, dedicated infra procurement, SLA changes.

High-level timeline (4-week pilot):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize sandbox target route, reserve GPU node, clone staging dashboards, onboarding call with feature team.
- Week 1 (instrument): add missing spans/metrics, validate traces, baseline synthetic profile.
- Week 2 (experiment): run a matrix of config changes (batch sizes, kv-cache enable/disable, quantization toggles), capture signals and error-budget events.
- Week 3 (automation): wire up automation hooks (canary rollback, model-variant fallback), run two end-to-end scenarios.
- Week 4 (synthesis): produce playbook, retro notes, remediation tickets.

Experiment design (notes / checklist):
- Sandboxes: create a sandbox namespace (sandbox-slo-pilot) with network isolation and a short-lived dedicated GPU pool (tagged).
- Traffic: use locust-based generator with three traffic profiles: short-chat (s1), long-completion (s2), batched-burst (s3). Profiles should mimic token distribution from product telemetry (sampled).
- Fault injection: CPU hog (10s spikes), GPU memory pressure (OOM knob), and network delay (100ms p50 to simulate cross-region). Tie each injection to an experiment label.
- SLIs to record: p50/p90/p99 latency (generation endpoint), token-level throughput, 5xx rate, model-fallback count, kv-cache hit rate, CPU/GPU utilization, grpc/HTTP retry counts, tail-queue-length.
- Synthetic SLOs for the pilot: availability >= 99.5 (on synthetic traffic), p99 latency < 850ms for short-chat, < 1500ms for long-completion. These are lab values for the exercise only.

Observability checklist (instrumentation tasks):
- Ensure request_id propagates into model runtime traces and KV cache layer.
- Add a span for batching waiting time and label by batch_size.
- Emit a metric for 'fallback_to_smaller_variant' with route and reason.
- Export token-generation-rate as a histogram (bucketed).
- Create dashboard panels: SLI timeline (by profile), per-batch latency breakdown (queue + compute + io), fallback events over time, resource heatmap.

Runbook snippet (simple playflow to validate):
1) Synthetic SLI breach detected -> runbook triggers 'verify experiment label' (ensure alert is from sandbox).
2) Check dashboard panel 'per-batch latency breakdown' and trace the offending request_id.
3) If unresponsive for >5m, trigger 'sandbox rollback script' which reverts config and restarts the route.
4) If degradation due to resource pressure, escalate to infra on-call to add burst node (sandbox-only).
5) Document incident in pilot journal and attach traces + exporters snapshot.

Automation hooks to prototype:
- Error-budget gate: when synthetic error budget for a schedule is exhausted, automatically pause new deployments for the route (via CI gating API).
- Auto-fallback: if p99 latency crosses threshold for two consecutive 1m windows, switch routing to a smaller model-variant and create a ticket.
- Canary rollback: a scripted rollback that flips canary weight back to 0% and runs smoke tests.

Roles & RACI (initial):
- Priya Shah (owner): pilot lead, coordinates cross-team.
- Ethan Morales (observability): dashboards, histograms, tracing spans.
- Asha Menon (serving-runtime): config toggles, fallback wiring, model variant endpoints.
- Diego Alvarez (platform/SRE): sandbox infra, node reservation, fault injection support.
- Maya Chen (product/feature): validates synthetic profiles map to product use cases.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Sandbox results don't reflect prod due to smaller scale. Mitigation: sample token distribution from prod and use stress multipliers; capture qualitative regression signals rather than absolute numbers.
- Risk: Automation accidentally touches prod. Mitigation: strong namespace isolation, RBAC checks, and an explicit safety flag required to target non-sandbox endpoints.
- Risk: Missing signals cause false negative. Mitigation: run a short 'observability smoke' checklist before experiment start.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: Which model route is the best single representative? (suggestion: text-gen-v2/chat-default).
- Q2: What minimum GPU spec is allowed for the sandbox? (T4 vs A10x).
- Q3: Do we back the error-budget gate with an on-call phone tree? For the pilot, likely not — scoped to automated CI gating only.

Artifacts to produce by pilot end:
- script: sandbox-run.sh (create namespace, deploy route clone, start traffic generator, apply fault profile)
- confluence: 'SLO Sandbox howto' with step-by-step and screenshots
- tickets: remediation backlog (obs gaps, instrumentation work, alert tuning)
- retro: lessons learned + decisions for production experimentation flow

Meeting cadence and workshops:
- Kickoff (30m): align owners and final route selection. - Target: 2026-11-17
- Daily 15m during experiment week (optional)
- Synthesis retro (60m) week after experiments complete

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Priya: confirm model route and schedule kickoff (action: schedule invite)
- Ethan: grab 48h of token distribution sample and draft traffic profiles (JIRA-REL-341)
- Diego: reserve sandbox GPU node and create namespace template
- Asha: check feasibility of exposing fallback metric in the runtime by 2026-11-22

Notes to self / informal scratchpad:
- Keep fail-safe flag in the sandbox deployment config: SANDBOX_SAFE=true
- Consider adding a cheap synthetic 'heartbeat' call at the start of each generated session to ensure warming is consistent
- Logging: rotate logs aggressively for sandbox to avoid long-term storage cost

Appendix: quick test scenario (copyable)
- Step 1: deploy cloned route 'text-gen-v2-sbx' with batch_size=16, kv_cache=true
- Step 2: start locust with profile s1 at 50 RPS for 10 minutes, collect p99 baseline
- Step 3: toggle batch_size=64 and re-run profile s1 for 10 minutes, run fault-injection CPU spike 30s at minute 3
- Step 4: validate p99 jump and confirm alert fires in alertmanager (sandbox group), then run rollback script

End of brief.

(Will convert to a one-pager and attach scripts once first run completes.)
